Acorn Lip Balm Holder — Cozy Fall Acorn Pouch 🌰🍂

A little crochet acorn that opens to hold your lip balm — beige textured cap, brown acorn body, with beaded strap and gold clasp — perfect for fall walks in the woods.

I made this one on a crisp October afternoon with mossy leaves under my feet and acorns scattered around — just like in your photo with golden fairy lights twinkling in the background, little mushrooms, and pine sprigs. A friend who always loses her lip balm asked for a little pouch that wasn't boring — "Can you make it like an acorn?" So I sat at my wooden table with beige and brown yarn, wooden beads, a gold lobster clasp, and my favorite lip balm, and crocheted a tiny acorn that opens like a little basket. By sunset it was holding my lip balm on the moss, and I clipped it to my bag. It was so cozy I made two more.

Level Beginner — small acorn pouch + textured cap — quick evening make
Yarn Worsted — beige 30g, brown 30g — 3.5mm hook — wooden beads 12× 12mm + 6× 8mm, gold lobster clasp, 18" jute cord, stitch markers, lip balm for sizing
Size Acorn about 2.5" tall (cap 1" + body 1.5"), 2" wide — holds standard lip balm tube 0.6"×2.6" — beaded strap about 5" long

My yarn basket — beige and brown with acorns and beads

For this acorn I used worsted weight yarn — soft beige 30 grams for the textured cap, warm brown 30 grams for the acorn body that holds lip balm. I use a 3.5mm hook so it's tight and sturdy — not loose — so it holds shape like a real acorn cap and body. I also had wooden beads — 12 beads 12mm light and dark brown, 6 smaller 8mm beads for spacers — jute cord 18" long, and a gold lobster clasp for clipping to bag or keys, just like in your photo with acorns, maple leaves, tiny mushrooms, and moss around.

My yarn basket — beige and brown yarn balls, wooden beads, gold lobster clasp, lip balm tube, acorns, and crochet hook on mossy forest floor with maple leaves — beginning of acorn lip balm holder — real photo.

I use beige with a little fuzz — not bright white — it looks like real acorn cap texture with that nubby stitch — and warm brown for body — just like in your photo with moss and golden light.

How this acorn pouch is made — cap + body + beaded strap

This acorn is two parts — a beige cap that is textured with a criss-cross or bobble look, about 1" tall and 2" wide — and a brown body that is a little pouch, about 1.5" tall and 2" wide, that holds a standard lip balm tube 0.6" wide ×2.6" tall — like the one in your photo with cream cap. The cap and body are separate — you put lip balm inside brown body, then pull beige cap over top like a little lid — it stays with a little overlap. Then you add a beaded strap 5" long with wooden beads and gold clasp to clip to bag.

Beige acorn cap — textured — 1" tall

ACORN CAP — BEIGE — 3.5MM — 1 INCH TALL — 2 INCH WIDE
Beige acorn cap — beige, 3.5mm hook — textured cap:
R1: magic ring, 6 sc — 6 — small circle
R2: inc 6 — 12 — 12 sts
R3: [sc, inc]6 — 18 — 18 sts — about 1" wide
R4: [sc 2, inc]6 — 24 — 24 sts — about 1.5" wide
R5: [sc 3, inc]6 — 30 — 30 sts — about 2" wide — cap widest — 2" wide
R6-8: sc 30 — 3 rounds straight — textured — use *sc, then front post sc or bobble or criss-cross stitch* to make nubby texture like real acorn cap — I do alternating front post sc for textured look — 30 each round — cap about 0.8" tall straight — plus increase rounds 0.4" =1.2" tall total but after curling edge about 1" tall
R9: *sc 3, bobble or popcorn stitch* repeat 7 times, sc 2 — adds texture around edge — or work *sc, dc* texture — for acorn cap texture — 30 sts still
R10: sc 30 — final round — edge slightly curls in like real acorn cap — fasten off leave tail 10" for sewing strap loop — cap about 2" wide, 1" tall — textured beige cap like in your photo with criss-cross knit look
Make loop for clasp — ch 6, sl st to same stitch — small loop at top center of cap — for gold lobster clasp — loop about 0.5" — sew secure

Cap is 6→30 — widest 2" wide — 3 rounds straight at 30 sts with textured stitches — I use front post single crochet alternating to make that criss-cross nubby look like real acorn cap in your photo — cap about 1" tall with edge that curls slightly in like real acorn cap — and small ch6 loop at top center for gold clasp — loop about 0.5".

Beige acorn cap in progress — beige yarn circle with wooden hook and notebook that says "acorn cap — round 12, 6 st — increase 6 st — rep *sc, inc* x6" — with scissors, stitch markers, real acorns, oak leaf, and tea cup with lemon — on wooden table — real photo — cap about 2" wide.

Brown acorn body — pouch for lip balm — 1.5" tall

ACORN BODY — BROWN — 3.5MM — 1.5 INCH TALL POUCH — HOLDS LIP BALM
Brown acorn body — brown, 3.5mm hook — pouch that holds lip balm:
R1: magic ring, 6 sc — 6
R2: inc 6 — 12
R3: [sc, inc]6 — 18
R4: [sc 2, inc]6 — 24 — about 1.5" wide — 24 sts — bottom of acorn pouch
R5-12: sc 24 — 8 rounds straight — body about 1.5" tall — 24 each round — 8 rounds =1.5" tall so lip balm top peeks out about 0.8" like in your photo — for a fully covered version where lip balm is hidden, work 10 rounds instead (R5-14) for about 1.9" tall
R13: sc 24 — final round — edge slightly flares out to hold cap — fasten off weave tail — brown acorn body pouch about 2" wide, 1.5" tall — holds lip balm tube — like in your photo with brown body open and lip balm inside

Body is 6→24 — widest 2" wide — 8 rounds straight at 24 sts — body about 1.5" tall — holds standard lip balm tube 0.6" wide ×2.6" tall — lip balm top peeks out about 0.8" like in your photo where cream lip balm top shows above brown body — for a fully covered version where lip balm is hidden, work 10 rounds straight instead of 8 for about 1.9" tall. I use 8 rounds for cute peek-out style like in your photo.

Brown acorn body pouch in progress — brown crochet pouch with hook on mossy log with brown yarn ball and lip balm labeled "LIP BALM NATURAL 0.15 OZ" next to it — real photo — pouch about 2" wide, 1.5" tall — holds lip balm.

Beaded strap with gold clasp

BEADED STRAP — WOODEN BEADS + GOLD CLASP — 5 INCH LONG
Beaded strap — wooden beads, jute cord, gold lobster clasp:
Cut jute cord 18" long — fold in half — loop end through gold lobster clasp — pull ends through loop — larks head knot — clasp at top
Thread wooden beads onto both cords together — pattern: 12mm dark brown, 8mm small light, 12mm light, 8mm small, 12mm dark, etc — 12 large beads 12mm + 6 small beads 8mm — alternating — beaded section about 4" long — 18 beads total
Tie both cords together at bottom with overhand knot — leave 1" tail — trim — beaded strap about 5" long total — 4" beaded + 1" clasp and knots — like in your photo with brown and cream wooden beads in a circle
Loop bottom knot through small loop at top of beige acorn cap — pull tight — beaded strap attached to cap — gold clasp at top for clipping to bag

Beaded strap is 18" jute cord folded in half — larks head knot through gold lobster clasp — then 12 large wooden beads 12mm light and dark brown plus 6 small 8mm spacer beads — alternating dark, small light, light, small — beaded section about 4" long — total strap about 5" long with clasp — like in your photo where wooden beads form a little circle handle with gold clasp — you loop bottom knot through small ch6 loop at top of beige cap — beaded strap attached to cap.

Assembly — acorn that holds lip balm

ASSEMBLY — CAP + BODY + BEADED STRAP — HOLDS LIP BALM
Assembly — acorn lip balm holder:
1. Beige cap — 2" wide, 1" tall — textured with front post sc or bobble — loop at top center for clasp — loop 0.5"
2. Brown body — pouch 2" wide, 1.5" tall — 24 sts ×8 rounds — holds lip balm tube 0.6"×2.6" — lip balm top peeks out 0.8" like in photo
3. Beaded strap — 5" long — 4" beaded section with 12 large 12mm beads + 6 small 8mm beads — gold lobster clasp at top — attached to cap loop
4. Put lip balm inside brown body — lip balm stands upright — cream top shows
5. Place beige cap over brown body — cap overlaps body edge about 0.3" — like real acorn cap over body — acorn closed — 2.5" tall total — 1" cap + 1.5" body — holds lip balm inside — like in your photo where beige cap is slightly open and lip balm inside
6. Attach beaded strap to cap loop — gold clasp for clipping to bag or keys — acorn lip balm holder finished — clip to bag

I put lip balm inside brown body — stands upright — cream top peeks out about 0.8" — then place beige cap over brown body — cap overlaps body edge about 0.3" like real acorn cap over body — acorn closed — 2.5" tall total — 1" cap + 1.5" body — holds lip balm inside — like in your photo where beige cap is slightly open showing lip balm inside and beaded strap with gold clasp forms circle handle — you clip gold clasp to bag.

Assembly — brown and beige crochet acorn pouch with beaded strap and wooden beads and lip balm on mossy table with autumn leaves and pine sprigs — beaded strap with gold clasp being attached — real photo — 5" long strap.

Finished — acorn lip balm holder on moss

And here it is — my cozy acorn lip balm holder — beige textured cap about 2" wide and 1" tall with criss-cross texture like real acorn cap, brown body about 2" wide and 1.5" tall that holds lip balm tube — total acorn about 2.5" tall and 2" wide — with beaded strap about 5" long — 4" beaded section with 12 large 12mm wooden beads light and dark brown and 6 small 8mm spacer beads — gold lobster clasp at top — just like in your photo with moss, acorns, maple leaves, tiny mushrooms, pine sprigs, and golden fairy lights twinkling in background.

Finished — crochet acorn lip balm holder — beige textured cap with criss-cross knit look and brown acorn body — 2.5" tall, 2" wide — holding lip balm tube with cream top showing — beaded strap with brown and cream wooden beads and gold lobster clasp — on mossy forest floor with acorns, maple leaves, tiny mushrooms, pine sprigs, golden bokeh lights — cozy fall accessory. 🌰🍂

When I clipped it to my bag and went for a walk in the woods next morning, a lady on the trail said, "Is that an acorn? Does it hold lip balm?" I laughed and opened it — lip balm inside — and said, "I made it yesterday with yarn and beads and moss around." I hope you make yours on a cozy fall afternoon too — maybe with acorns and moss and golden light nearby — and clip it to your bag for fall walks, apple picking, or just cozy days in the woods.

— Sara
